newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia diesel rebounds after hitting near term floor.
newsitem.headline: Asia diesel rebounds after hitting near term floor.

text.p: Ramthan Hussain

Asian diesel price has hit a near-term floor as some buyers emerged to take advantage of cheap oil but the market remained gloomy as demand was insufficient to absorb the abundant stocks, traders said on Friday.
"It blew my mind when prices came down under $22.00 this week, prompting an excellent buy at $21.45 (on Wednesday)," a trader with a European refiner said.
"But pending another drop on crude this is already a bargain for gas oil and even in the short term there should be a lot of bargain hunters looking for discount values and distress cargoes."
Traders said sellers are still targetting the Chinese market, despite persistent talk that inventories on the mainland and Hong Kong are high.
They said the cheap cargoes were too good for China to resist, with talk that buyers are targetting to buy as low as $155 per tonne, cost-and-freight southern China.
While sellers were still trying to offer at $170 per tonne, c-and-f basis, traders said any potential demand would not be overlooked.
For example, one Chinese trader has bought at least three cargoes over the past week--one from Singapore and two from Northeast Asia--to take advantage of the low prices.
China's scattered interest came about despite concerns that China might continue to clamp down on imports due to the high stocks and to encourage endusers to buy oil products from local refineries.
Regional diesel prices started to slump below $22.00 early last week from more than $25.00 in early June. It hit a low of $21.45 on Wednesday, but started to rebound marginally on Thursday to $21.60.
The recovery continued to be seen on the swaps market on Friday with July being quoted at $22.20/$22.40, up 25 cents from Thursday and 70 cents from Wednesday.
Traders believe the market would pick up in August, which explained the contango with July/August spread seen at 40 cents per barrel.
Physical prices on a floating prices basis are currently assessed around a 20-cent discount to Singapore quotes.

The weak market forced Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) to defer floating its term diesel export tender until after August. "The actual date to issue the tender will depend on market situation," a CPC source said.
Instead, Taiwan issued a spot tender to sell 225,000-250,000 barrels of diesel for July 23-27 lifting, which closes June 26.

Traders said the additional cargo offered for July would add on to the well-supplied market, which was already being weighed down by a stock build in Singapore of 339,000 barrels to 11.575 million barrels for the week ended June 18.

The bears in the market pointed out to unpredictable demand from Indonesia despite shutdowns at Balikpapan and Cilacap in July and August respectively as Indonesia was said to have suffcient stocks to cover any shortages.

Traders said Indonesia's monthly diesel import during that period could be limited to three million barrels, with most being sourced from its term contract. Indonesia was now said to be negotiating with a US trader for a 90,000 tonne cargo for July.
India's spot demand for August was also expected to be curbed because it has a six-month term tender with the first delivery in August.
-- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
